[[File:6Loops-Brunnian-link.svg|thumb|More complex Brunnian link of six loops, based on illustration in Brunn's 1892 paper]]
'''Karl Hermann Brunn''' (1 August 1862 – 20 September 1939) was a German [[mathematician]], known for his work in [[convex geometry]] (see  [[Brunn–Minkowski theorem|Brunn–Minkowski inequality]]) and in [[knot theory]]. [[Brunnian link]]s are named after him, as his 1892 article "Über Verkettung" included examples of such links.

==Life and work==
Hermann Brunn was born in [[Rome]], and grew up in [[Munich]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Kjeldsen|first=T.H.|authorlink= Tinne Hoff Kjeldsen |title=Egg-forms and measure-bodies: different mathematical practices in the early history of the modern theory of convexity.|journal=Sci. Context|year=2009|volume=22|issue=85–113|pages=85–113|doi=10.1017/S0269889708002081|s2cid=122788987 }}</ref> He studied mathematics and physics at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]], graduating in 1887 with the thesis ''Über Ovale und Eiflächen'' (About ovals and eggforms).<ref>{{cite book|last=Brunn|first=H.|title=Über Ovale und Eiflächen|year=1887|publisher=Akademische Buchdruckerei von F. Straub|location=Munich}}</ref> He habilitated in 1889.
